headline: Chile Becomes First South American Country to Eliminate Dog-Transmitted Rabies
meta_description: Chile has achieved a historic milestone by eliminating dog-transmitted rabies, marking decades of sustained public health commitment across the region.
summary_short: Chile has become the first South American country to eliminate dog-transmitted rabies to humans, a landmark achievement recognized by the World Health Organization.
body:
Chile has become the first South American country to eliminate dog-transmitted rabies to humans, marking a historic milestone in public health. The World Health Organization announced this validation, recognizing the nation's decades-long commitment to protecting its communities.

This achievement reflects a broader regional success: human cases of dog-transmitted rabies across the Americas have plummeted by more than 98% since 1983. The dramatic decline demonstrates what sustained investment in vaccination programs and public health infrastructure can accomplish.

According to WHO Director-General Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus, Chile's validation reflects the power of long-term dedication to prevention and community protection. The milestone offers hope that other nations in the region can follow Chile's path toward eliminating this deadly disease entirely.
quick_facts: Chile is the first South American country to eliminate dog-transmitted rabies
Dog-transmitted rabies cases in the Americas dropped over 98% since 1983
WHO validated Chile's achievement after decades of public health investment
